evidence_excerpts: if being F grounds being G, our account implies that being G just is being F or H for some given H, and which on our account gives the (or a) full essence of being G. It then follows that necessarily, a thing is G iff it is F or H, which entails by straightforward modal reasoning that necessarily, a thing is F only if it’s also G, as desired.
text: If being F grounds being G, then the fact that being F necessitates being G can be derived from what it is to be G.
